title: Nightshift mini-lit scratches: kv-cache, selective-batching, & fidelity checks
content:
Context / why I skimmed these tonight:

- Follow-up after the kv-sharding spike: want to find lightweight cache formats that preserve retrieval fidelity while allowing mixed quantized kernels. Low-cost paths for long-context chat apps are high priority for the demo next month.
- Quick goal: identify 2 implementable ideas I can prototype this sprint (8 engineering-hours each).

Papers & posts I skimmed (short takes):

1) "Compressed Key-Value Representations for Streaming Prefixes" (preprint, Apr 2029)
- Claim: reduce KV memory by ~3x using a delta-encoded quantized residual over chunked prefixes.
- Core trick: represent older KV segments as compact deltas relative to a low-precision summary vector; reconstruct when needed with a small correction network.
- Practical notes: looks heavier on CPU for reconstruction; good candidate when hot prefix locality is very high and misses are rare.
- My read: promising if we can amortize reconstruction across batch boundary; not great for very low-latency per-request paths unless we do background warmups.
- Experiment idea: implement a toy delta-compress->reconstruct loop in Python+JAX; measure wall-time for reconstruct on a single A100 vs CPU.

2) "Selective Batching: latency-aware micro-batching for heterogeneous workloads" (conference talk notes + slides)
- Claim: mixing tiny micro-batches with opportunistic coalescing reduces tail latency without losing throughput on bursty traffic.
- Scheduler idea: keep a tiny fast-path queue for requests with strict SLOs and a coalescing queue with a 3–10ms window for best-effort requests; dynamically float requests across tiers based on recent SLO violations.
- My read: aligns with our smart routing/fallback goals; could slot into the edge scheduler in Dedicated.
- Implementation idea: augment the existing request router with a two-tier queue and a short coalescing timer; start with simulation using our traces (use trace slice: april-2029/ping-logs).

3) "Fidelity probes for low-precision sampling" (blog + appendix experiments)
- Claim: a set of lightweight synthetic probes can detect when quantization shifts sampling distribution enough to materially change downstream behavior (e.g., hallucination rate or repetition).
- Probe types: n-gram stability, next-token surprise delta, and prompt-anchored recall tests.
- My read: we should plug a small probe suite into Optimize to auto-tag models/configs that need higher-precision fallbacks for specific prompt types.
- Quick script: implement 3 probes and run against our eval bucket of 200 prompts; compare fp16 baseline vs 4-bit quantized variant.

Rapid synthesis / actionable next steps:

- Prototype 1 (8–12h): "delta-kv toy"
  - Goal: minimal delta compress + reconstruct loop.
  - Inputs: random prefix KVs from test-model-2 (cache dumps).
  - Outputs: compression ratio, reconstruct latency, memory-on-device, and sample decode difference metric (perplexity on held prompts).
  - Where to put it: experimental repo /repos/kv-experiments/ (create README).

- Prototype 2 (8h): "two-tier scheduler sim"
  - Use existing trace simulator (sim/trace-player). Implement two queues, coalescing window param, and dynamic float heuristic (float up if > p95 lateness).
  - Metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput, percent of requests in fast-path.

- Prototype 3 (6h): "probe-suite against quantized configs"
  - Implement 3 probes (ngram-stability, surprise-delta, recall-anchor). Run fp16 vs 4-bit vs 3-bit configs and produce small report.

Open questions / risks:

- Reconstruction compute cost might be dominated by memory bandwidth on GPU; if so, delta-kv is only viable for cold-prefix eviction and not for on-the-fly accesses. Need microbenchmarks.
- Selective batching requires accurate request classification; if we misclassify, SLOs can get worse. Where to get labels? Use client-route metadata and historical latencies.
- Probes are heuristics; need to pick thresholds carefully to avoid false positives that force costly fallbacks.

Short TODOs (next 48h):

- [ ] Create repo skeleton for kv-experiments and add README + small script to load sample cache dumps (assign Arun).
- [ ] Pull 24 hours of production-like traces from trace-store (ask SRE for access, ticket ENG-SRE-456).
- [ ] Implement probe scripts and run quick baseline against model-x-small on CPU quantized weights (I will do this Monday night).
- [ ] Sync with Lina about edge-scheduler constraints and where this could slot into Dedicated (quick sync tomorrow).

Notes-to-self / random thoughts:

- If delta-reconstruct is expensive but infrequent, consider edge-tier: keep last N tokens fully materialized on device and store older compressed segments in a local SSD/DRAM on host; reconstruct in background when predicted-to-be-used.
- Could we combine selective batching with probe triggers? e.g., if probe detects degraded fidelity while using 4-bit, auto-migrate that route to fast-path micro-batching or full-precision instances.
- Add simple AB test in staging: run quantized+probes vs baseline on small traffic slice and measure both latency and a simple hallucination metric (keyword-presence).

References / links I flagged:

- arXiv:2903.12345 (delta-kv preprint)
- slides: selective-batching-nyc-2029.pdf (downloaded)
- blog: quant-fidelity-probes (notes + code snippet)

If someone reads this and wants to pick up an item: ping me or drop a quick note in #research-quickwins. I expect to have an initial probe script and the sim changes as PR prototypes by end of next week.
